correctness.rationale: Exact expansion of the ambiguity separates a p-root chirp term and exactly L_u positive root summands. Prime cyclotomic divisibility gives the modular obstruction, while k<p/3 gives 0<L_u<p, proving all Fourier pixels nonzero. Galois norm gives lower bound; Weyl diagonalization yields normalized lifting singular values. Complete finite exact checks for 5,7,11 and sampled other primes plus three explicit boundary zeros corroborate the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Natural Gabor tomography design problem: tolerance of a linearly growing number of arbitrarily placed unit-amplitude site impurities with a single simple complex chirp seed. The cross-term overlap count is the structural invariant, sufficient density and stronger modular test are explicit, and examples separate robust and failing regimes. Not merely a single parameter or routine finite census.
